records.source: Λοιπὸν οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ἐρωτῶμεν ὑμᾶς καὶ παρακαλοῦμεν ἐν κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ, ἵνα καθὼς παρελάβετε παρ’ ἡμῶν τὸ πῶς δεῖ ὑμᾶς περιπατεῖν καὶ ἀρέσκειν θεῷ, καθὼς καὶ περιπατεῖτε, ἵνα περισσεύητε μᾶλλον.
records.gloss: Finally then, brothers, we ask you and urge in [the] Lord Jesus, that just as you received from us the how it is necessary you to walk and to please God, just as also you walk, that you abound more.
pieces: Finally, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we ask you and urge you in the Lord Jesus: you learned from us how you ought to live to please God, and you are living that way. Now do so more and more.

L.1: Finally then, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we ask and urge you in [the] Lord Jesus that, just as you received from us how you ought to walk and to please God, as indeed you are walking, you should abound [in this] more.

R.1: And now, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we have something more to say. We taught you how to live in a way that pleases God, and you are already living that way. Now we ask you, as people who belong to the Lord Jesus, to do this even more.

decisions.choice: finally then: as for the rest
decisions.reason: Λοιπὸν marks a turn to the next subject, not the end: two chapters follow (compare Philippians 3:1).

decisions.choice: received: took over what was handed on
decisions.reason: παραλαμβάνω is the word for receiving teaching handed down (2:13; Colossians 2:6).

decisions.choice: to walk and to please God: one way of life
decisions.reason: "Walk" is the biblical picture for how one lives (2:12); living rightly and pleasing God are one thing.

decisions.choice: in the Lord Jesus: as those who belong to him and speak for him
decisions.reason: Paul's appeal carries the Lord's authority (verse 2).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: live
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a figure for how one lives; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: And now ... we have something more to say
decisions.reason: "Finally" would suggest the letter is ending (m1).

records.heading: A life that pleases God

records.source: οἴδατε γὰρ τίνας παραγγελίας ἐδώκαμεν ὑμῖν διὰ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: You know for what instructions we gave you through the Lord Jesus.
pieces: You know what instructions we gave you by the authority of the Lord Jesus.

L.2: For you know what instructions we gave you through the Lord Jesus.

R.2: You know the teachings we gave you. They came from the Lord Jesus.

decisions.choice: instructions: commands given with authority
decisions.reason: παραγγελίας was used of orders passed down a chain of command.

decisions.choice: through the Lord Jesus: on his authority
decisions.reason: The instructions came from the Lord through Paul and his companions.

decisions.choice: by the authority of
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "through the Lord" means here (m2).

records.source: τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, ὁ ἁγιασμὸς ὑμῶν, ἀπέχεσθαι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τῆς πορνείας, εἰδέναι ἕκαστον ὑμῶν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σκεῦος κτᾶσθαι ἐν ἁγιασμῷ καὶ τιμῇ, μὴ ἐν πάθει ἐπιθυμίας καθάπερ καὶ τὰ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ εἰδότα τὸν θεόν, τὸ μὴ ὑπερβαίνειν καὶ πλεονεκτεῖν ἐν τῷ πράγματι τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, διότι ἔκδικος κύριος περὶ πάντων τούτων, καθὼς καὶ προείπαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ διεμαρτυράμεθα.
records.gloss: This for is [the] will of the God, the holiness of you, to abstain you from the sexual immorality, \v 4 to know each of you the of himself vessel to control in holiness and honor, \v 5 not in passion of desire just as also the Gentiles the [ones] not knowing the God, \v 6 the not to transgress and to wrong in the matter the brother of him, because [an] avenger [is the] Lord concerning all these [things], just as also we told before you and solemnly warned.
pieces: This is God's will for you: that you be holy. Keep away from sexual immorality.
Each of you should know how to keep your own body under control, with holiness and respect,
not in lustful passion like the Gentiles, who do not know God.
In this matter no one must cross the line and wrong a {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}, for the Lord avenges all such things, as we told you before and solemnly warned you.

L.3: For this is the will of God, your holiness: that you abstain from sexual immorality;
L.4: that each of you know how to control his own vessel in holiness and honor,
L.5: not in the passion of lust like the Gentiles who do not know God;
L.6: that no one transgress and wrong his {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} in this matter, because [the] Lord is an avenger in all these things, as we also told you before and solemnly warned [you].

R.3: God wants you to be holy. He wants you to stay away from every kind of sexual sin.
R.4: Each of you should learn to control your own body, so that you live in a way that is holy and right.
R.5: Do not let strong sexual desires control you, as they control people who do not know God.
R.6: No one should wrong a fellow believer or cheat them in this. We told you before and warned you strongly: the Lord will punish people who do these things.

decisions.choice: this is the will of God, your holiness: explained by what follows
decisions.reason: ὁ ἁγιασμὸς stands beside "the will of God" and names it; the infinitives that follow (abstain, know how, not wrong) say what holiness means here.

decisions.choice: holiness: being made holy, set apart for God
decisions.reason: ἁγιασμός is both the process and the state of being made holy. It comes three times in verses 3-7.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: any sexual relationship outside marriage
decisions.reason: πορνείας is the general word for sexual sin (Colossians 3:5). The Greek and Roman world around them accepted much that the gospel rejected.

decisions.choice: control one's own body
decisions.reason: σκεῦος means a vessel or container. It can stand for the body (2 Corinthians 4:7), and κτάομαι ("acquire") can mean to gain mastery of: "learn to control your own body". But "vessel" was also used of a wife (compare 1 Peter 3:7), and "acquire a vessel" for marrying: "learn to take a wife for yourself in holiness". On the first reading Paul speaks to all; on the second, to the men.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles who do not know God
decisions.reason: The phrase echoes Jeremiah 10:25 and Psalm 79:6. The Thessalonian believers were themselves Gentiles (1:9), but now know God; they are not to live as they once did.

decisions.choice: in this matter: in sexual conduct
decisions.reason: ἐν τῷ πράγματι could mean business, and πλεονεκτέω ("take advantage") often goes with greed. But the whole passage is about sexual holiness: wronging a fellow believer here means violating their marriage or family.

decisions.choice: the Lord is an avenger: Psalm 94:1
decisions.reason: God is "the God of vengeance" who puts wrongs right (Psalm 94:1; Deuteronomy 32:35). "The Lord" may be God or Jesus as judge.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} (L, B); a fellow believer (R)
decisions.reason: The wrong can be done to any believer, man or woman; "brother" is the traditional form. Readable's "fellow believer" needs no setting.

decisions.choice: your own body
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense chosen in m4, which is uncertain; Literal keeps "vessel".

decisions.choice: Do not let strong sexual desires control you
alternatives: not in the passion of lust
decisions.reason: Readable puts "the passion of lust" in plain words.

records.source: οὐ γὰρ ἐκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς ὁ θεὸς ἐπὶ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ ἀλλ’ ἐν ἁγιασμῷ.
records.gloss: Not for called us the God for impurity but in holiness.
pieces: For God did not call us to be impure, but to live in holiness.

L.7: For God did not call us to impurity but in holiness.

R.7: God did not call us to live in an impure way. He called us to be holy.

decisions.choice: not for impurity but in holiness
decisions.reason: ἐπὶ marks the purpose God did not have; ἐν the sphere in which he called them: their calling took place in holiness and leads to it.

decisions.choice: to live in holiness (B); He called us to be holy (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what being called "in holiness" means.

records.source: τοιγαροῦν ὁ ἀθετῶν οὐκ ἄνθρωπον ἀθετεῖ ἀλλὰ τὸν θεὸν τὸν καὶ διδόντα τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ τὸ ἅγιον εἰς ὑμᾶς.
records.gloss: Therefore the [one] rejecting not a human rejects but the God, the [one] also giving the Spirit of him the Holy to you.
pieces: So anyone who disregards this is setting aside not a human command but God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, the God who gives you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Holy Spirit.

L.8: Therefore whoever rejects [this] rejects not a human being but God, who also gives {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Holy Spirit to you.

R.8: So if anyone refuses to obey this teaching, they are not refusing a person. They are refusing God, the one who gives you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: reject: set aside as not binding
decisions.reason: ἀθετέω means to set aside or treat as invalid.

decisions.choice: who gives his Holy Spirit to you: Ezekiel 36:27; 37:14
decisions.reason: God promised through Ezekiel to put his Spirit within his people so that they would walk in his ways. The present participle διδόντα says God goes on giving the Spirit, the source of holiness.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "who gives his Holy Spirit to you"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "gave" for "gives", and some "us" for "you". The meaning is close either way.

decisions.choice: not a human command but God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
alternatives: not a human being but God
decisions.reason: Balanced says what is being set aside.

records.source: Περὶ δὲ τῆς φιλαδελφίας οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε γράφειν ὑμῖν, αὐτοὶ γὰρ ὑμεῖς θεοδίδακτοί ἐστε εἰς τὸ ἀγαπᾶν ἀλλήλους·
records.gloss: Concerning now the brotherly love, no need you have [for anyone] to write to you, yourselves for you taught by God are to love one another;
pieces: About love for one another as {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you do not need us to write to you, because God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} has taught you to love each other.

L.9: Now concerning love for the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you have no need [for anyone] to write to you, for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another.

R.9: You do not need anyone to write to you about loving your fellow believers. God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} has taught you to love each other.

decisions.choice: love for the brothers and sisters: love within the family of believers
decisions.reason: φιλαδελφίας is love for one's brothers, used in the church for love among believers, who are one family (Romans 12:10).

decisions.choice: taught by God: the promise that God himself would teach his people
decisions.reason: θεοδίδακτοί is first found here. It recalls Isaiah 54:13 ("all your children will be taught by the LORD") and Jeremiah 31:33-34 (John 6:45).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The love is for all believers, women and men; "brothers" is the traditional form.

records.heading: Love and quiet work

records.source: καὶ γὰρ ποιεῖτε αὐτὸ εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς τοὺς ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Μακεδονίᾳ.
records.gloss: And indeed you do it toward all the brothers the [ones] in all the Macedonia.
pieces: And in fact you do love all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} throughout Macedonia.

L.10: And indeed you are doing it toward all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} throughout Macedonia.

R.10: And you are already showing this love to all the believers everywhere in Macedonia.

decisions.choice: all Macedonia: the churches of the province
decisions.reason: Other churches in Macedonia included Philippi and Berea (Acts 16-17).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

records.source: παρακαλοῦμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, περισσεύειν μᾶλλον, καὶ φιλοτιμεῖσθαι ἡσυχάζειν καὶ πράσσειν τὰ ἴδια καὶ ἐργάζεσθαι ταῖς χερσὶν ὑμῶν, καθὼς ὑμῖν παρηγγείλαμεν, ἵνα περιπατῆτε εὐσχημόνως πρὸς τοὺς ἔξω καὶ μηδενὸς χρείαν ἔχητε.
records.gloss: We urge but you, brothers, to abound more, \v 11 and to aspire to be quiet and to do the own [things] and to work with the hands of you, just as you we commanded, \v 12 so that you may walk properly toward those outside and of no one need you may have.
pieces: But we urge you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, to love more and more.
Be eager to live calmly, look after your own affairs and earn your living with your hands, as we instructed you,
so that outsiders will see you live rightly, and you will not need to rely on anyone.

L.10: But we urge you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, to abound [in it] more,
L.11: and to make it your ambition to live quietly and to mind your own affairs and to work with your hands, as we instructed you,
L.12: so that you may walk properly toward outsiders and have need of no one.

R.10: But we encourage you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, to love each other even more.
R.11: Try hard to live a quiet, peaceful life. Take care of your own work, and earn your living with your own hands, as we told you before.
R.12: Then people who are not believers will respect the way you live, and you will not have to depend on anyone.

decisions.choice: make it your ambition to be quiet: a deliberate paradox
decisions.reason: φιλοτιμέομαι means to seek honor, to be ambitious; Paul joins it to ἡσυχάζω, to be quiet. Their ambition should be a calm, ordered life.

decisions.choice: work with your hands
decisions.reason: Paul had worked with his hands among them (2:9). Some in the church seem to have stopped working (5:14; 2 Thessalonians 3:6-12), perhaps because they expected the Lord to come soon or because they relied on wealthier believers; the letter does not say why.

decisions.choice: need of no one
decisions.reason: μηδενὸς can be masculine ("no one") or neuter ("nothing"). Either way, their work would keep them from being a burden on others.

decisions.choice: walk properly toward those outside: live in a way that outsiders respect
decisions.reason: εὐσχημόνως means decently, becomingly. "Those outside" are unbelievers (Colossians 4:5).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: to love more and more (B); to love each other even more (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what they are to abound in: love (verses 9-10).

decisions.choice: outsiders will see you live rightly (B); people who are not believers will respect the way you live (R)
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a figure for how one lives (m4).

records.source: Οὐ θέλομεν δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, περὶ τῶν κοιμωμένων, ἵνα μὴ λυπῆσθε καθὼς καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ οἱ μὴ ἔχοντες ἐλπίδα.
records.gloss: Not we want and you to be ignorant, brothers, concerning those sleeping, so that not you grieve just as also the rest, the [ones] not having hope.
pieces: We do not want you to be left in the dark, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, about those who have fallen asleep, so that you do not grieve as others do who have no hope.

L.13: And we do not want you to be uninformed, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, about those who are asleep, so that you may not grieve as the rest do, who have no hope.

R.13: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, we want you to understand what happens to believers who have died. Then you will not be sad like other people, who have no hope.

decisions.choice: those who are asleep: believers who have died
decisions.reason: "Sleep" was a common way of speaking of death (John 11:11-13; Acts 7:60). For believers it carries the hope of waking: they will rise (verse 16).

decisions.choice: not grieve as those who have no hope: grief with hope, not no grief at all
decisions.reason: Paul does not forbid grief; he says their grief is different from that of people who have no hope of resurrection.

decisions.choice: the occasion: some believers had died
decisions.reason: Since Paul left, some members of the young church had died. The others seem to have feared that those who died would miss the Lord's coming. Verses 14-17 answer that fear.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: believers who have died
decisions.reason: Readable says what "sleep" means here (m1).

records.heading: Those who have fallen asleep

records.source: εἰ γὰρ πιστεύομεν ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἀπέθανεν καὶ ἀνέστη, οὕτως καὶ ὁ θεὸς τοὺς κοιμηθέντας διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἄξει σὺν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: If for we believe that Jesus died and rose, so also the God those having fallen asleep through the Jesus will bring with him.
pieces: We believe that Jesus died and rose again; and in the same way, through Jesus, God will bring with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} those who have fallen asleep.

L.14: For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also God will bring with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, through Jesus, those who have fallen asleep.

R.14: We believe that Jesus died and came back to life. So we also believe that, through Jesus, God will bring back with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the believers who have died.

decisions.choice: if we believe: since we believe
decisions.reason: εἰ states what is true of them: they do believe it.

decisions.choice: Jesus' resurrection guarantees theirs
decisions.reason: οὕτως καὶ ("so also") draws the conclusion: as God raised Jesus, so he will raise those who belong to him (1 Corinthians 15:20-23).

decisions.choice: through Jesus: goes with "God will bring"
alternatives: goes with "have fallen asleep": those who died as believers in Jesus
decisions.reason: διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ stands between the two verbs. It may say how God will bring them, through Jesus, or describe the dead as those who "fell asleep through Jesus", that is, in faith in him. Either way they belong to him.

decisions.choice: bring with him: when Jesus comes, the dead come with him
decisions.reason: Verse 16 explains how: they rise first and so share in his coming.

decisions.choice: the believers who have died
decisions.reason: Readable says what "fallen asleep" means (verse 13).

records.source: τοῦτο γὰρ ὑμῖν λέγομεν ἐν λόγῳ κυρίου, ὅτι ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες οἱ περιλειπόμενοι εἰς τὴν παρουσίαν τοῦ κυρίου οὐ μὴ φθάσωμεν τοὺς κοιμηθέντας·
records.gloss: This for to you we say by [a] word of [the] Lord, that we the living, the remaining until the coming of the Lord, by no means will precede those having fallen asleep;
pieces: On the Lord's own authority we tell you this: those of us still living, who remain until the Lord comes, will in no way get there before those who have fallen asleep.

L.15: For this we say to you by a word of [the] Lord: that we who are alive, who are left until the coming of the Lord, will certainly not go ahead of those who have fallen asleep.

R.15: What we are telling you comes from the Lord: when the Lord comes, those of us who are still alive will not go to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} before the believers who have died.

decisions.choice: by a word of the Lord: a teaching that comes from the Lord Jesus
alternatives: a message revealed to Paul by the risen Lord
decisions.reason: This may be a saying of Jesus not recorded in the Gospels in these words (compare Matthew 24:30-31), or a word given to Paul by the risen Lord. Either way, Paul's comfort rests on the Lord's authority, not on his own guess.

decisions.choice: we who are alive: Paul counts himself among those who may be living
decisions.reason: Paul speaks as one who might be alive when the Lord comes, but he sets no date (5:1-2), and elsewhere he speaks of himself as one who will be raised (2 Corinthians 4:14).

decisions.choice: will certainly not go ahead of
decisions.reason: οὐ μὴ is the strongest way to say "not": the living will have no advantage over the dead.

decisions.choice: coming: the Lord's arrival
decisions.reason: The word used for the visit of a ruler (2:19).

decisions.choice: On the Lord's own authority
alternatives: by a word of the Lord
decisions.reason: Balanced states what "a word of the Lord" gives this teaching (m1).

decisions.choice: go to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} before the believers who have died
alternatives: go ahead of those who have fallen asleep
decisions.reason: Readable says what "go ahead of" means here (verse 17).

records.source: ὅτι αὐτὸς ὁ κύριος ἐν κελεύσματι, ἐν φωνῇ ἀρχαγγέλου καὶ ἐν σάλπιγγι θεοῦ, καταβήσεται ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐν Χριστῷ ἀναστήσονται πρῶτον, ἔπειτα ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες οἱ περιλειπόμενοι ἅμα σὺν αὐτοῖς ἁρπαγησόμεθα ἐν νεφέλαις εἰς ἀπάντησιν τοῦ κυρίου εἰς ἀέρα· καὶ οὕτως πάντοτε σὺν κυρίῳ ἐσόμεθα.
records.gloss: because himself the Lord with a shout of command, with [the] voice of an archangel and with [the] trumpet of God, will descend from heaven, and the dead in Christ will rise first, \v 17 then we the living, the remaining, together with them will be caught up in clouds for [the] meeting of the Lord in [the] air; and so always with [the] Lord we will be.
pieces: The Lord {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will come down from heaven at a shout of command, at an archangel's call and the sound of God's trumpet, and the dead who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will rise first.
Then those of us still living, who are left, will be swept up with them into the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. From then on we will be with the Lord always.

L.16: For the Lord {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will descend from heaven with a shout of command, with [the] voice of an archangel and with [the] trumpet of God, and the dead in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} will rise first;
L.17: then we who are alive, who are left, will be caught up together with them in [the] clouds to meet the Lord in the air; and so we will always be with [the] Lord.

R.16: The Lord {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will come down from heaven. There will be a loud command, the voice of a chief angel, and the sound of God's trumpet. Then the believers who have died will come back to life first.
R.17: After that, those of us who are still alive will be taken up with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. Then we will be with the Lord forever.

decisions.choice: a shout of command
decisions.reason: κελεύσματι is a cry of command, used of an officer's order or a signal.

decisions.choice: an archangel: a chief angel
decisions.reason: ἀρχαγγέλου is used in the New Testament only here and in Jude 9, where Michael is named. There is no article: "an archangel's voice".

decisions.choice: the trumpet of God
decisions.reason: A trumpet sounded when God came down on Sinai (Exodus 19:16) and will sound when he gathers his people (Isaiah 27:13; Matthew 24:31; 1 Corinthians 15:52).

decisions.choice: the dead in Christ will rise first: before the living are caught up
decisions.reason: "First" answers the Thessalonians' worry (verse 15): the dead are not left behind but rise before the living are gathered with them (verse 17).

decisions.choice: will be caught up: snatched up suddenly
decisions.reason: ἁρπάζω means to seize or snatch away (Acts 8:39). The Latin Bible's word here, "rapiemur", is where the word "rapture" comes from.

decisions.choice: to meet the Lord: like a city going out to welcome an arriving ruler
decisions.reason: ἀπάντησιν was used when a city's people went out to meet an important visitor and escort him in; Acts 28:15 uses it of believers coming out of Rome to meet Paul. This may suggest that believers go out to meet the Lord as he comes, though the word itself does not settle where they go next.

decisions.choice: in the clouds: the clouds of God's presence
decisions.reason: The Son of Man comes with the clouds (Daniel 7:13), and Jesus was taken up in a cloud and will come in the same way (Acts 1:9-11).

decisions.choice: always with the Lord: the heart of the hope
decisions.reason: The passage ends not with details of the events but with what matters most: the living and the dead together, with the Lord for ever.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: swept up
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the suddenness of the verb (m5).

decisions.choice: the believers who have died
decisions.reason: Readable says who "the dead in Christ" are.

records.source: ὥστε παρακαλεῖτε ἀλλήλους ἐν τοῖς λόγοις τούτοις.
records.gloss: Therefore encourage one another with the words these.
pieces: So comfort one another with these words.

L.18: Therefore encourage one another with these words.

R.18: So use these words to comfort and encourage each other.

decisions.choice: encourage: comfort and strengthen
decisions.reason: παρακαλέω covers both comfort and encouragement; after grief (verse 13), comfort comes first.
